role.altitude: The service unit operator keeps directing the crew, running the unit and judging what happens downhole; writing readings into the tour report by hand and counting collars on strip charts shrink.
skills_to_grow: Checking recorder data before it goes into the tour report
role.ambitious_version: An operator whose reports fill themselves from the unit's recorder, so the evening goes to planning the next day.

tasks.short: Hold the pre-job safety talk, direct drilling crews assembling and connecting pipe, applying weights to drill pipes and drilling around lodged obstacles, record the work in the tour report and report to the client's representative.

steps.what: Operator holds the pre-job safety talk with the crew
Operator directs drilling crews assembling and connecting pipe
Operator directs applying weights to the drill pipe while watching the weight indicator
Operator directs the crew drilling around lodged obstacles
Operator writes the crew's work, depths, weights and hours in the daily tour report
Operator reports progress and problems to the client's site representative

tasks.design: Directing the crew stays fully hands-on, and no software takes part in decisions on the rig floor. The only change: on units with a data recorder, the tour report is a tablet form that takes depth, hook load and pressure readings from the recorder per activity, and the operator adds what the crew did and the hours worked.
tasks.previous_blocker: Readings were copied from gauges and charts into a paper tour report at the end of the shift.
tasks.enabler_now: Rig data recorders export readings that a tablet form can take in.
tasks.human_edge: Feeling through the brake that the pipe is about to stick.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes on the floor; the report takes less writing.

reach.learn: Whether recorder readings in the report answer questions the engineer used to phone about.

evidence.claim: Rig data recorders log depth, hook load and pump pressure and can export them.
Hours per crew member in a digital report can monitor presence and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: directing the crew during a job; planning the job is the engineer's work.

Input contract for s5: readings exported by the unit's data recorder, fitted on about 60% of units; units without a recorder keep the paper report. On recorder units the depth, hook load and pressure readings fill in, while the crew's work and hours stay first writes, so s5 keeps 75 overall. Checking the export against the gauge is the incremental entry, not part of s5.
Directing and safety talks keep their full time.
unknowns: Which units carry a data recorder.
research_questions: Do tour reports with recorder readings cause fewer disputes with the client?

incremental.description: Operator checks the recorder export matches the gauge before signing the report.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only a third of units carry a working recorder, so most tour reports stay on paper (1.0); high: recorders on about 60% of units as assumed (2.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review the job program, rig up and apply technologies such as coiled tubing or gas lift systems, run the operation watching pressures and loads, adjust with the engineer and record job data.

steps.what: Operator reviews the job program for the coiled tubing or gas lift job
Operator rigs up the coiled tubing unit or gas lift equipment at the well
Operator applies the technology: runs the coiled tubing or gas lift operation watching pressures and loads on the unit's control screen
Operator adjusts rates and pressures with the well engineer
Operator records depths, rates and pressures of the job in the job report

tasks.design: The operation itself stays with the operator on the unit's own controls; no software is added to the control loop. The job report is filled from the unit's data acquisition log of depth, rates and pressures, and the operator adds the sequence of events and remarks.
tasks.previous_blocker: Job data were read off screens and charts and written up by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Coiled tubing units log job data that can fill a report.
tasks.still_hard: Running the unit safely under pressure.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing that the injector head is not running right.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in running the job.

reach.learn: Whether logged job data replace notes in the job report.

evidence.claim: Coiled tubing units record depth, weight and pressures during a job.
No AI Act high-risk area applies to a report filled from logged data.

assumptions: Boundary: running the job on site; designing the job is the engineer's work.

Input contract for s5: the data acquisition log written by the unit during the job, on about 80% of units; older units keep the handwritten report. The operator still writes the sequence of events and remarks, so s5 keeps 50 overall. Checking the log export is the incremental entry, not part of s5.
Rig-up, running and adjusting keep their full time.
unknowns: How many jobs per month use coiled tubing or gas lift.
research_questions: Do engineers use the logged data more than the written report?

incremental.description: Operator checks the log export before closing the report.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only half of units have a usable data log, so more reports are handwritten (2.7); high: about 80% of units log the job (4.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Connect the acoustic sounder to the wellhead, fire the shot, monitor sound wave-generating and detecting mechanisms to determine well fluid levels, record the result and judge it against earlier shots.

steps.what: Operator connects the acoustic gun and microphone to the wellhead
Operator fires the shot and monitors the sound wave-generating and detecting mechanisms as the echo is recorded
Operator reads the echo trace and counts tubing collar reflections to determine the fluid level
Operator records the fluid level and well data: on the well test sheet today; after the change the sounder software fills the shot record and strip chart results are typed
Operator checks the final shot record: well, date, fluid level and that the level fits the trace
Operator releases the checked shot record to the production database for the production engineer
Operator judges the result against earlier shots and tells the engineer about changes

approvals.approved_version: The shot record with well, date and fluid level exactly as checked by the operator in s4c, released once to the production database for that well; any correction needs a new check.

tasks.design: A digital acoustic sounder records the echo on a laptop, where its software counts collar reflections against the tubing tally and computes the fluid level with fixed formulas; the operator checks the trace on screen. The software fills each shot record with well, date and fluid level; the operator checks it and releases it once to the production database, so nothing is copied onto a test sheet. Connecting the gun, firing it and judging changes stay with the operator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Strip charts were read by hand and results copied onto paper sheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital acoustic sounders compute fluid levels and export shot records.
tasks.still_hard: Noisy traces and wells with paraffin or foam.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising a false echo from a liner top.
tasks.altitude: Less counting and copying; the operator still judges each shot.

reach.learn: Whether shot histories in the database lead to earlier pump changes.

evidence.claim: Digital acoustic well sounders count collar reflections and compute fluid level in software.
No AI Act high-risk area applies to fluid level measurement records.

assumptions: Boundary: one fluid level shot from connecting to reporting; pump changes are the engineer's work.

Input contract for s3: the echo trace recorded by the digital sounder and the tubing tally from the well file kept by the production engineer; about half of crews still use strip chart sounders, which keep hand counting; s3 is priced at that share.
Input contract for s4: the sounder software fills each shot record; strip chart results are typed, so s4 keeps 50. The check and release of each record keep their full time.
Connecting, firing and judging keep their full time.
research_questions: How often does the operator overrule the software's collar count?

already_counted.description: Operator checks software collar counts on noisy traces.

incremental.description: Operator keeps tubing tallies in the sounder software current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: three quarters of crews still use strip chart sounders, so most counting and typing stays (9.5); high: about half use digital sounders as assumed (19.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
